Vision and Values
This mission statement encapsulates the school's dedication to academic excellence, character development, and community engagement, reflecting its vision for educating young learners.
Our school values can be summarised in the word SHINE:
Here's a brief explanation for each value:
These values together create a positive and empowering school culture where everyone can SHINE.
Honesty
Inclusivity
Our School
Vision and Values

Welcome
We are delighted to welcome you to Stanhope Primary School.
Stanhope Primary School is a brand new primary school that collaborates with our vibrant learning community where children are at the heart of everything we do. We are proud to be part of the Engage Enrich Excel Academies (EEEA) Trust.
We were thrilled to welcome our founding classes of reception children in September. It was truly a special moment to be part of the school's very first cohort.
Thank you for your enthusiasm and patience as we have brought this fantastic new school to life. We are really enjoying being part of this exciting journey with your children.
“Education is not the learning of facts, but the training of the mind to think.”
Our School

Early Years
Our Curriculum is designed to reflect the interests and needs of our children and to immerse our children in a language rich environment. We prioritise high quality interactions with adult focussed activities where appropriate. Our children guide and drive their own learning through carefully resourced continuous provision with enhancements to aid the development of skills and knowledge. Our curriculum is unique to us and our children's needs at Stanhope Primary School.
Our curriculum is developed to prioritise sequential, progressional learning, where pupils know more and can do more, building on what they have been previously taught. It is also designed to be responsive to the needs of our children, families and community.
Each topic planned, is individually tailored to our children each year, with the aim of ensuring that all children leaving Reception are ready to start the KS1 curriculum. Topics do not always last a specific amount of time but are developed based on the children’s learning at the time and the related core knowledge and skills which need to be taught. All topics are carefully resourced and where possible are introduced with a high quality, diverse story book or age appropriate non – fiction text that reflects the interests and experiences of our children.
Our ambitious Early Years curriculum aims to teach all children the skills and knowledge in order that they reach the seventeen Early Learning Goals described in the Early Years Foundation Stage framework. Our staff are highly skilled and confident with assessing necessary starting points based on quality baselining interactions. Staff know their children well and quickly recognise those who will need early intervention due to entering our setting with low starting points. They monitor who is and is not on track regularly, put in timely catch-up sessions and tailor future planning to provide more opportunities for skill development and progress.
As many of our activities as possible are play-based, however there is also a need for some direct teacher-led activities to ensure all children gain essential knowledge and skills. When appropriate, activities are expertly modelled using Rosenshine's 10 principles of instruction (I do, we do, you do). Priority is given to providing sufficient sustained periods of play with support and resources to allow children to repeat and deepen their taught skill development.
We use Birth to Five Matters as a rich resource to support our knowledge of child development and as a supporting document for our curriculum. We feel that this document reflects our early years vision of embedding quality interactions in a variety of playful situations. It supports our staff to create organic learning opportunities as opposed to being constrained by formal expectations.

Curriculum
At EEEA, we create primary curriculums that are designed to inspire and engage our students while adhering to the standards set by the National Curriculum. We believe that a well-rounded education is crucial for developing curious, knowledgeable, and well-prepared individuals. Our curriculum is meticulously crafted to spark a love for learning in every child, encouraging them to explore a wide range of subjects with enthusiasm and confidence.
We set high expectations for both our students and our staff, ensuring that every lesson is delivered with excellence and every child is supported to reach their full potential. Our dedicated teachers employ innovative teaching methods and resources to make learning exciting and relevant, helping students to connect what they learn in the classroom to the world around them. This approach not only enhances academic achievement but also fosters critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills.
By integrating the National Curriculum with our own high standards, we aim to provide a challenging yet supportive learning environment. We continuously assess and refine our curriculum to ensure it meets the evolving needs of our students and society. Our goal is to equip our students with the knowledge, skills, and values they need to succeed in their future endeavors, fostering a lifelong love of learning and a commitment to excellence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stanhope Primary School - Free School Meals and Pupil Premium
pageCache.text:
Free School Meals and Pupil Premium
All children in Year R, Year 1, and Year 2 are entitled to universal free school meals which do not need to be applied for. Additionally, children whose parents meet the criteria below are eligible for Pupil Premium funding which provides vital funds for the school. Children eligible for this funding will also be able to continue to receive free school meals once they reach year 3.
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
Support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
The guaranteed element of Pension Credit
Child Tax Credit (providing you are not also entitled to Working Tax Credit, with an annual gross income of no more than £16,190)
Working Tax Credit run-on (paid for four weeks after you stop qualifying for Working Tax Credit)
Universal Credit (for applications made on or after 1 April 2018, your household income must be less than £7,400 a year, after tax, and excluding any benefits received)
If you think your child may be eligible for Pupil Premium funding please use the following link to apply FSM/Pupil Premium Application

School Dinners
Our school dinners are provided by Chartwells and the menus are on a 3-week rotation. There is always a main option, a vegetarian option, a jacket potato and a sandwich every day. All our meals are served with vegetables or fresh salad and are suitable for those following a Halal diet.
Your child's teacher will help them to make a selection from the menu each morning. The current menus are below if you would like to discuss the options with your child.
